input.description: Find webhook delivery and SSRF protection code
input.prompt:
In this repository, find where the server sends outbound HTTP webhook/notification requests to external systems when content changes (e.g. a "webhook delivery" or "notify" function that does an HTTP POST to a user-configured URL). 

I need:
1. The exact file path and function name that performs the actual outbound HTTP request (the fetch/axios/http.request call for delivering the webhook payload).
2. Any code that protects against SSRF (server-side request forgery) — i.e., validation that blocks the webhook URL from pointing at internal/private/loopback network addresses (like 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.x, 192.168.x, etc.), including file path and function/mechanism name.

Search terms to try: "webhook", "notify", "dispatch", "deliver", SSRF, "isPrivate", "private IP", "internal IP", "ipaddr", "blocked", "dns lookup", URL validation for webhooks.

Report back file paths and relevant code snippets/line numbers for both the delivery function and the protection mechanism.

content.text:
h02.

delivery function — `Post` (and its async wrapper `PostAsync`) in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (uses the package-level `safeClient` HTTP client, initialized at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:32`, to do the actual `http.NewRequest`/`safeClient.Do` POST to the webhook URL); dispatch is triggered from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` and `server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` when memo content changes.

protection mechanism — `internal/webhook/validate.go`: `ValidateURL` (line 62) rejects webhook URLs that resolve to reserved/private IPs at creation time, using `isReservedIP`/`reservedNetworks` (lines 14–54, covering loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/cloud IMDS 169.254.169.254, and IPv6 equivalents). At actual delivery time, `internal/webhook/webhook.go`'s `safeDialContext` (line 59, wired into `safeClient`'s `Transport.DialContext` at line 35) re-resolves the hostname and blocks connections to any reserved/private IP at dial time — this is what defeats DNS-rebinding attacks that could bypass the create-time-only `ValidateURL` check.
